To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cytoplasmically exposed surfaces of gap junctions in rat heart and liver differ in ultrastructural appearance.
the cytoplasmically exposed surfaces of cardiac gap junction particles have a fuzzy layer of protein subunits, while the cytoplasm of liver gap junction particles does not.
in situ cardiac gap junctions have a fuzzy CS coating that is not found in situ in liver gap junctions and is lost when cardiac gap junctions are proteolyzed or isolated with PMSF.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of gap junction proteins and their assembly into gap junctions.

the structure and function of gap junctions, intercellular channels that are present in many tissues, and which allow the direct exchange of ions, small molecules, and electrical current between adjacent cells.
the molecular organization of gap junctional proteins and with the structural differences in gap junctions in different tissues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, at least in rat, the CS components of heart gap junction proteins are more complex than those of liver gap junctions, and the CS of in vivo and isolated heart junctions are more complex than that of isolated liver junctions.

the CS of unproteolytic isolated junctions is particulate in heart and nonparticulate in liver, whereas the CS of isolated proteolyzed cardiac and liver junctions and the CS of in-situ junctions are non-particulate.

the CSs of unproteolytic isolated cardiac gap junctions and in situ cardiac gap junctions contain a urea-resistant, fuzzy coating, while the CSs of proteolytic isolated cardiac junctions and in vivo and in vitro isolated liver junctions do not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cytoplasmically exposed surface of heart junctions is fuzzy, whereas that of liver junctions is not, and that the cytoplamsic surface of proteolyzed cardiac gap junctions is particulate, whereas the CS of unproteolytic heart junctions is not.(ABSTRACT TRUNCATED AT 250 WORDS)

the CS of unproteolytic, isolated, deep-etched cardiac junctions is particulate and urea resistant and that of proteolytic, isolated cardiac junctions is nonparticulate and urea sensitive, while the CS of liver junctions is non-particulate and ureasensitive, regardless of whether they are isolated or in situ.

in situ gap junctions have a fuzzy CS layer, that this is removed during isolation, and that the isolated junctions have a CS that is particulate in the case of unproteolytic cardiac junctions and nonparticulate in the case that the junctions are proteolytic or liver.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytoplasmically oriented gap junction proteins of cardiac and hepatic cells have different structures.
the CS of cardiac junctions are different from liver and in situ junctions.
there are differences between the gap junctions of the heart and liver.
